drivingQuestion: Why does David call the psalm of his flight from Absalom a psalm rather than a lament?
outcomeNote: the parable and its application settle why the psalm is a מזמור; nothing is raised against it

segments.he: ״מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד בְּבָרְחוֹ מִפְּנֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם בְּנוֹ״, ״מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד״?! ״קִינָה לְדָוִד״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
segments.en: Regarding the opening phrase of the psalm, which serves as its title, the Gemara wonders: It is said: «“A Psalm of David, when fleeing his son, Absalom.” A Psalm of David? It should have» said: «A lament of David.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֲבִישָׁלוֹם: מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה? — לְאָדָם שֶׁיָּצָא עָלָיו שְׁטַר חוֹב. קוֹדֶם שֶׁפְּרָעוֹ הָיָה עָצֵב, לְאַחַר שֶׁפְּרָעוֹ שָׂמַח.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shimon ben Avishalom said a parable: To what is this similar?» It is similar «to a person about whom a promissory note was issued» stating that he must repay a debt to the lender. «Before he repaid it,» he «was despondent,» worried how he will manage to repay the debt. «After he repaid it, he was glad.»

segments.he: אַף כֵּן דָּוִד, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: ״הִנְנִי מֵקִים עָלֶיךָ רָעָה מִבֵּיתֶךָ״, הָיָה עָצֵב, אָמַר: שֶׁמָּא עֶבֶד אוֹ מַמְזֵר הוּא, דְּלָא חָיֵיס עֲלַי. כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּאַבְשָׁלוֹם הוּא — שָׂמַח. מִשּׁוּם הָכִי אֲמַר ״מִזְמוֹר״.
segments.en: «So too» was the case with «David. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, told him,» through Natan the prophet, after the incident with Bathsheba, «“Behold, I will raise up evil against you from your house”» (II Samuel 12:11), David «was despondent. He said: Perhaps» it will be «a slave or a mamzer» who will rise up in my house, a person of such lowly status, who «will have no pity on me. But once» David «saw that Absalom was the one» through whom the prophecy was to be fulfilled, «he rejoiced,» as he was certain that Absalom would show him mercy. «That is why» David «said a psalm,» not a lament, thanking God for punishing him in the least severe manner possible.

moves.summary: the Gemara presses on the psalm's title, cited in the preceding unit, as the wrong word for the occasion
moves.about: why the psalm of David's flight from Absalom is headed 'a psalm' and not 'a lament'

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמעון בן אבישלום: משל למה הדבר דומה?
moves.summary: he answers with the parable of a man who is despondent while a promissory note stands against him and glad once he has paid it
moves.about: why David sang rather than lamented when Absalom rose against him — a parable of a debtor who is glad once the note is paid

moves.summary: the parable is applied: David feared a slave or a mamzer would rise against him, and rejoiced to see it was Absalom, who would pity him
moves.about: Natan's prophecy of evil arising from David's own house, the decree David feared
